bibliographic.title: The Agentic AI Framework (AAIF): a policy-enforced architecture for accountable and high-performance intrusion detection
bibliographic.authors: Ibrahim Adabara; Bashir Olaniyi Sadiq; Aliyu Nuhu Shuaibu; Yale Ibrahim Danjuma; Venkateswarlu Maninti; Mutebi Joe
bibliographic.citation_apa: Adabara, I., Sadiq, B. O., Shuaibu, A. N., Danjuma, Y. I., Maninti, V., & Joe, M. (2026). The Agentic AI Framework (AAIF): a policy-enforced architecture for accountable and high-performance intrusion detection. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 9, 1755696. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1755696

methodology.study_design: Framework design, implementation, and evaluation using a benchmark intrusion-detection dataset
methodology.sample_description: CICIDS2017 network intrusion dataset with over 2.8 million network flow records across benign and malicious traffic
methodology.technology_context: Deep learning-based intrusion detection integrated with a YAML-based policy engine, audit ledger, and governance metrics aligned to NIST AI Risk Management Framework 2.0

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study proposes and evaluates a policy-enforced deep learning intrusion detection framework in cybersecurity; it does not address conversational AI, chatbots, agents in dialogue, RAG, or LLM-based systems in regulated conversational environments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the article strongly addresses AI governance, accountability, auditability, and policy compliance, its core system is a network intrusion detection pipeline using deep learning on CICIDS2017. The review scope targets conversational governance in LLM-based systems in regulated settings. Provided text shows no conversational interface, no LLM application, and a cybersecurity rather than regulated-sector conversational context. Governance concepts are present but not in the target phenomenon.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Title uses 'Agentic AI' and automated triage scored highly on governance terms; manual confirmation is needed to avoid misclassifying a cybersecurity IDS paper as central conversational LLM governance evidence.

appraisal.notes: Internally, the study presents a clear DSR-based framework with quantitative detection and governance metrics. Transferability to conversational LLM governance in regulated domains is limited based on the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: Claims appear coherent and supported for cybersecurity IDS governance, but relevance to conversational LLM governance in regulated environments is very low because the evidenced system is deep learning intrusion detection, not conversational or LLM-based.

coding.subtheme: Intrusion detection with executable governance constraints

synthesis.main_claim: AAIF integrates deep learning intrusion detection with a YAML-based policy engine and audit mechanisms to preserve detection performance while achieving full policy and ethical compliance.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a reproducible policy-enforced architecture and governance metrics demonstrating accountable autonomy without degrading IDS performance on CICIDS2017.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpts do not detail study limitations; evaluation is confined to one cybersecurity benchmark dataset and non-conversational IDS use case.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational LLM governance; optionally cite only as peripheral contextual reference for policy-schema and audit-loop design patterns if the review permits non-conversational governance analogies.
